articles.summary: Amazon's Prime Big Deal Days doesn't officially begin until October 6, but we're already seeing some early discounts ahead of the two-day shopping event, including savings across Philips' Sonicare electric toothbrush range.
body: There are several models currently reduced at Amazon UK, ranging from the more affordable Sonicare 2100 Series to the considerably fancier DiamondClean Prestige 9900. So, whether you're looking to make the switch from a manual toothbrush or simply fancy upgrading your current one, there are a few options worth checking out before Prime Big Deal Days properly gets underway.

The Philips Sonicare 2100 Series is currently £44 at Amazon UK, making it the cheapest option in this particular selection and a relatively straightforward entry point if you've never used an electric toothbrush before.
It delivers 31,000 bristle movements per minute and has two intensity settings, Medium and Low, alongside a programme designed to ease you into using an electric toothbrush over your first week.
There's also a two-minute timer to help you brush for the recommended amount of time, while Philips says the battery can last for up to 14 days between charges.

articles.title: 26 years ago, 'Buffy the Vampire Slayer's Worst Season Premiere Redefined a Legendary Villain
articles.summary: Ever since, Dracula has evolved into an enduring figure, often treated as the final boss in most vampiric tier lists. Dracula has appeared in everything from Nosferatu (1922) to Blade (1998). He typically symbolizes a grand threat that must be defeated before it's too late.
body: Vampires in fiction can be traced back to the 18th century, but these undead stock villains only became a fleshed-out archetype in Bram Stoker’s 1897 gothic horror, Dracula. In Stoker’s book, the Count is a layered metaphor for social taboos and pestilence, while his move from Transylvania to England presents themes of xenophobia.

The season 5 premiere of Buffy the Vampire Slayer, however, doesn’t treat Dracula with such reverence. Titled “ Buffy vs. Dracula,” the episode features Buffy Summers (Sarah Michelle Gellar) being confronted by Count Dracula (Rudolf Martin), who unceremoniously appears in Sunnydale to seek out the renowned Slayer.

“Get out!” Buffy retorts with skepticism after her first meeting with the Count, initially dismissing him as a “fanboy” like the countless vampires who “call themselves Lestat.” The rest is an expectedly campy showdown between the Slayer and the Count, turning “Buffy vs. Dracula” into a fun, albeit lackluster season premiere.
points: Ever since, Dracula has evolved into an enduring figure, often treated as the final boss in most vampiric tier lists.

articles.title: Spider-Man Star Tom Holland's Next Film Adds Sabrina Carpenter To Its Cast
articles.summary: Following the record-breaking success of Spider-Man: Brand New Day and The Odyssey, Tom Holland is preparing to star in his next film, a biopic about Fred Astaire. Now, we've learned that he will co-star alongside Sabrina Carpenter and Margaret Qualley in that movie.
body: If you're unfamiliar with Fred Astaire, he's a prolific dancer and stage and movie star who you'd probably recognize from classic musicals like Top Hat, Swing Time, and The Band Wagon. Holland has a dancing and theater background, so he has been trying to get this biopic off the ground for some time. Now, in the wake of two big hits, Tom Holland is finally making the movie with Paul King, a director best known for Wonka and the recent trilogy of Paddington films.

On Sept. 25, Deadline reported that Sabrina Carpenter and Margaret Qualley joined the cast. Carpenter will play actress Ginger Rogers, while Qualley will portray Fred's sister Adele Astaire. Speaking to Deadline about the casting, King said, "The cinematic challenge of bringing to life these icons of the twentieth century is one that I could not imagine without Tom Holland, Margaret Qualley and Sabrina Carpenter by my side."

articles.title: Magic: The Gathering Meets D&D-Style Dice Battles in the Best New TCG at PAX West 2026
articles.summary: 2026 has been, in several crucial ways, an HD remake of the late '90s and early 2000s. My old boot-cut jeans are inexplicably back in fashion, live-action Spider-Man and Resident Evil movies are hitting theaters, no one will shut up about Wolverine, and the last nerd convention I went to hosted a…
body: At PAX West in Seattle, most of that battle unfolded inside Summit, the newer of the Washington State Convention Center's two buildings. Its tabletop floor featured official booths for Riftbound, OverPower, Rush of Ikorr, and the Gundam Card Game. In previous years, it had struck me that Magic: The Gathering had more or less taken over the TCG space, at least at PAX. Now there are multiple contenders visibly gunning for its throne.

One of the more interesting challengers, however, was hiding a few blocks away. The World of Kylia booth was half-hidden in the Arch building's expo hall. Here, the local Washington company iQ Pictures was showing off their card game Ascendant, which just celebrated its second anniversary.

According to its creator, Chase Lambert-Crittenden, the world of Kylia as a whole began as a side project while he was working towards an animation degree in California. Kylia is an inhabitable world in a distant galaxy, which naturally produces a valuable plasma-like substance called Genki. In the present day, Kylia is home to multiple native and alien species, who exist alongside one another in seven separate nations.

articles.title: Control Resonant Violates the Number One Commandment of Video Game Lore
articles.summary: So much of Control, Remedy Entertainment’s 2019 paranatural shooter, sticks with me today, but the one thing I really remember is its lore. Its setting, a Brutalist Manhattan office building called The Oldest House, is littered with paperwork covered in black redactions, so much of which explains…
body: It makes sense, then, that Remedy would double down on what it did best for Control Resonant. Though the sequel takes the series out of The Oldest House and onto the Hiss-infected streets of Manhattan, protagonist Dylan Faden still stumbles upon plenty of notes and audio logs left behind in an apocalyptic event. But what should be a selling point for Resonant is one of its minor pain points: There’s just too much lore to sift through.

That’s not a knock against the quality of Remedy’s writing, mind you; every piece of lore I’ve found in Resonant so far is top-notch. Something as simple as a tuning fork puzzle in a subway gets elevated by notes that paint a picture of a frustrated research team trying to understand why they keep teleporting around. It makes every piece of Resonant ’s world feel narratively motivated rather than something that’s there for the sake of gameplay. That’s what puts Remedy head and shoulders above so many of its peers as a big-budget developer.

articles.title: Marvel's Wolverine Dev Adds Option to Turn Off Controversial Scent Trails and More in New Update
articles.summary: Insomniac Games has published a new Marvel's Wolverine update that adds an option to turn off those controversial scent trails for collectibles.
body: The Sony developer made good on its promise to investigate a proper on/off option when version 1.001.006 launched just hours ago. Its patch notes reveal more targeted changes as the studio works out the remaining kinks that have emerged in the days since Marvel's Wolverine launched for PlayStation 5.

There are three new toggle settings that players can now use to customize their gameplay experience: one for Whiskey Bottle scent trails, one for Material Crate Audio Clues, and one for Nightmare Door Roots. Those first two proved to be an especially hot topic online, with players criticizing in-game hints as one of a few examples of a game many feel is too 'hand-holdy.' Adding the option to completely turn these guides off should quiet those concerns, with a toggle for Nightmare Door Roots adding even more freedom for players to tailor their Marvel's Wolverine experience to their liking.

The new toggles are pretty straightforward. If players find the wavy visuals to be a bit too distracting, they can simply turn them off. As noted in the in-game settings, using Wolverine's Crate Finder and Whiskey Finder Adaptations will override any flipped toggles.

articles.title: MobyGames video game database now lets developers claim their game credits
articles.summary: Video game database MobyGames will let developers claim video game credits and customise their personal portfolios, albeit only via a new premium tier.
body: As reported by our sister site GamesIndustry.biz, MobyGames Professional launched in beta in June, with a full 1.0 version due this autumn. Alongside enabling developers to claim credits of games they've worked on via a verification process, it also lets users build a personal portfolio page on the site.

Talking specifically about the verification process behind claiming a page, which stops short of letting anyone edit their actual credit listings, Denzel said: "There's two parts to that. One is making sure that people are who they say they are, and that's a human-driven verification process that we run in the background. When it comes to making sure that credit history is reflected appropriately, the actual way that we do credits and credit verifications has not changed: It's not changed since Atari has been involved, it's not changed in a long time, and we have no plans to change that process". Atari acquired MobyGames in March 2022.

articles.title: US court orders Redditor to pay Nintendo £3.4m over Switch piracy
articles.summary: A US District Judge has granted Nintendo a £3.4 million ($4.5m) default judgment against James Williams, the former Reddit moderator known online as "Archbox", after he failed to respond to a lawsuit over alleged Nintendo Switch piracy.
body: After putting Switch pirate Gary Bowser behind bars and targeting emulator software Yuzu, back in 2024 Nintendo hunted down alleged Switch pirate James "Archbox" Williams, the main moderator behind r/SwitchPirates, by tracking his Reddit posts.

By this time last year, court papers revealed Nintendo was seeking $4.5m in damages from Williams, accusing him of having "facilitated a network of unauthorised 'shops'...that have offered to the public extensive libraries of pirated Nintendo Switch games for download".
And now, according to TorrentFreak, $4.5 million (£3.4m) is exactly what Williams now owes Nintendo.
The judge noted that while Williams had not responded to the lawsuit, he must have been aware of it given he had hired a lawyer to object to a Google subpoena.

articles.title: Microsoft CEO says Xbox's 'streamlining' process is 'great to see' following its most recent round of layoffs
articles.summary: Earlier this week, Xbox laid off 268 people on top of the 1,600 jobs it cut earlier this year. It has shoved Obsidian into Bethesda, handed Halo to Activision, said Sayonara to Double Fine and Compulsion Games, and State of Decay developer Undead Labs, and is primed to close Hellblade developer…
body: All of this is part of Xbox's "reset", under its new(ish) CEO Asha Sharma. Sharma has been the public face of the company's deeply controversial restructuring, defending it with statements like "great technology gets better when it gets simpler, not bigger" which, incidentally, is why aeroplanes always perform better when you rip one of the wings off.

But both Sharma and Xbox are ultimately part of a much larger organisation. So what does Microsoft's head honcho Satya Nadella think of all these cuts, closures, and cancellations? Well, he thinks that Xbox's "streamlining" is "great to see".

Speaking on the Sources Podcast with Alex Heath (via Kotaku ), Nadella briefly touched upon the subject of the Xbox layoffs as part of a much wider-ranging interview, starting by gassing up all the intellectual property that Xbox has under its belt. "I feel fantastic about the IP we have right now," Nadella stated. "If I look at the studios, the IP portfolio we have, and our ability to then take that and produce great games going forward, I feel fantastic."

articles.title: It took CD Projekt two years to design Phantom Liberty's Chimera Tank boss fight: 'We were iterating over and over'
articles.summary: One of the most striking early sequences in Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty is its Chimera Tank boss fight, in which V and President Myers battle an enormous, Ghost in the Shell-inspired spider-tank in the bowels of a Barghest facility.
body: Speaking on CD Projekt's official AnsweRED podcast (via Eurogamer ), Phantom Liberty's game director Gabe Amatangelo, and creative director Igor Sarzyński discussed various production challenges the studio faced during Cyberpunk 2077 's creation, bringing up the Chimera Tank as an example. "Sometimes we're making content that's a nexus point of different disciplines, the Chimera is a great example of that," Amatangelo said. "It was gameplay, narrative, art, worldbuilding."

According to Paweł Mielniczuk, Phantom Liberty's art director and the podcast's co-host, creating the boss fight was a years-long process. "I think when we were iterating, it was two years to make this boss fight work," he explained. Later in the chat, Mielniczuk stated the tank went through "four" different iterations that involved "changing equipment [and] the weapons", while Sarzyński claimed that the Chimera's construction represents "one of the most expensive art assets I think ever."

articles.title: Former Starfield designer says Bethesda's sci-fi RPG probably won't get a sequel, because the original wasn't 'anywhere near successful enough'
articles.summary: I wasn't expecting to see a Starfield sequel any time soon, given it took Bethesda eight years to make its sci-fi RPG and the studio is currently focussed on The Elder Scrolls 6.
body: In an interview with FRVR (via VGC ), Bethesda veteran Kurt Kuhlmann explained why he doubts the studio will ever return to Starfield: "I would be very surprised", said Kuhlmann, who left Bethesda after Starfield was released. "I don't think Starfield was anywhere near successful enough to do a Starfield 2."

While specific sales figures for Starfield haven't been released, Bethesda's sci-fi RPG is estimated to have generated $300 million in revenue as of April this year. This would make Starfield profitable based on its reported budget of $200 million, but it still has a long way to go before it reaches Skyrim levels of success. Since Xbox has reportedly expressed a desire to focus on its major franchises, it seems likely that Bethesda will prioritise The Elder Scrolls and Fallout over Starfield.

Nonetheless, Kuhlmann thinks this may represent a missed opportunity for Bethesda to build on the lessons learned creating Starfield and create something truly special: "It's in a way, too bad, because I think with the lessons learned on Starfield, a Starfield 2 could have been much closer to the game that Todd had [in mind]."
points: I wasn't expecting to see a Starfield sequel any time soon, given it took Bethesda eight years to make its sci-fi RPG and the studio is currently focussed on The Elder Scrolls 6.

articles.title: After Warcraft 3's first new campaign in 23 years, let's normalize releasing new DLC for ancient RTS games
articles.summary: Age of Empires and Blizzard's RTS offer a playbook for how to keep the nostalgia fires burning.
body: The recent trend of announcing new expansions for older games—most notably Songs of the Past for The Witcher 3 —makes total sense when you look at the long tail on some of yesterday's classics. Beloved games now have a tendency to stick around for so long that new blockbusters are fighting for their lives against perennial Steam favourites that look like they could've been released yesterday.

The likes of Cyberpunk 2077 and Baldur's Gate 3 aren't going anywhere, for example, and both would be great candidates for all-new DLC in 10 or so years because people will probably still be talking about them. Quake is a much older game, but its recently added episode is part of the same trend. So too is the newly-revealed Thief campaign in Nightdive's upcoming remaster.

Exciting as these expansions are, it's more thrilling to me when a real-time strategy game gets the same treatment. Is this because I love real-time strategy games? Yes. But it's also because the genre has a slightly different relationship with nostalgia.
points: Age of Empires and Blizzard's RTS offer a playbook for how to keep the nostalgia fires burning.

videos.title: Ariadne's Tale - Announcement Trailer | PS5 Games
videos.summary: Step into Ariadne's Tale, a first-person puzzle adventure that reinvents the classic myth with wit and dark humour. As Ariadne, you carry a magical thread that guides your path and serves as a tool to fix routes, anchor points and activate mechanisms.
body: Each chamber is a test of observation and creativity: combine puzzle solving, object manipulation and lateral thinking to progress. The narrative blends ironic voices with a mythic atmosphere: an architect guides (and nags) you through a magical conch, while the terror and beauty of the Labyrinth slowly unfold. The goal is clear: find and rescue Theseus… before the threads of fate are cut.
points: Step into Ariadne's Tale, a first-person puzzle adventure that reinvents the classic myth with wit and dark humour.
As Ariadne, you carry a magical thread that guides your path and serves as a tool to fix routes, anchor points and activate mechanisms.
Use the thread to orient yourself, manipulate devices and reach the heart of the Labyrinth before the beast finds you.
Each chamber is a test of observation and creativity: combine puzzle solving, object manipulation and lateral thinking to progress.
